## Problem and relation to the other three notebooks

This fourth added-mean convergence study complements the three restored
smooth experiments. It combines a dedicated centered rough
run with its exact constant mode, rather than restoring an archived
nonzero-mean rough run. All nine exponents
$\alpha=0.9,\ldots,1.7$ and all meshes of the mean-zero rough study are retained.
The connected tadpole has stem length 1, loop length 2, and total length 3.
We solve
$$
 u_t+\nu(-\Delta_\Gamma)^{\alpha/2}u=1+g,\qquad u(s,0)=1,
 \qquad\kappa=0,
$$
with continuity and Kirchhoff conditions, where
$$
 g=\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-1}\phi_j,\qquad
 \phi_j=0\text{ on the stem},\qquad
 \phi_j(x)=\sin(2^j\pi x)\text{ on the loop }[0,2].
$$
The rough part is unchanged: $g\in L_2$ but has no positive spectral
Sobolev regularity. Since every $\phi_j$ has zero spatial mean,
$$
 u_{\rm added}(s,t)=u_{\rm rough,zero}(s,t)+1+t,
 \qquad\bar u(t)=1+t,\qquad M(t)=3(1+t).
$$
Adding a smooth constant changes neither the forcing's rough regularity
nor the centered fractional diffusion. It does supply mass at rate 3.

## Running and knitting

Run setup, parameters, and the computation chunk manually to save results.
Knitting only loads that saved file, checks its parameters, and displays
results. The computation chunk has `eval=FALSE`; missing or incompatible
results stop knitting without launching a solver.

By default the manual computation recomputes the centered rough PDE at
the refined settings, saving it to this experiment's own centered file.
It then adds the exact constant component as explained below. To reuse
that centered file on a later run, set `recompute_centered <- FALSE`;
all scientific parameters must still match. The mean-zero study's files
are unchanged. Worker count affects execution only. Internal checks belong
in `DOCS/NAP`.

```{r nonzero-mean-rough-setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,error=FALSE,cache=FALSE,
                      dev="png",fig.width=8,fig.height=5)
if(!requireNamespace("ggplot2",quietly=TRUE)) stop("Install ggplot2 for figures.")
```

## Explicit full-run parameters

The rough forcing, $J=5:9$, $K=16$, $J_\star=18$, $\nu=1$,
and $\gamma_*=1/3$ are retained. Relative to the first added-mean run,
the solver time step decreases tenfold to $8\cdot10^{-8}$, reference
time step decreases to $5\cdot10^{-6}$, and rational order increases
from 14 to 16. These changes target the high-alpha, fine-mesh temporal
floor. The sampled norm and the full constant error are retained.
A maximum mean squared-error fraction of 0.02 is enforced in the
experiment, so that the mean increases the centered error by less than
about 1.02%. This budget does not replace independent time-refinement
checks, which remain in `DOCS/NAP`.

The rational order 16 passes the coefficient admissibility conditions for
all nine exponents in the installed tables. Higher orders are not assumed
to be available uniformly. This full run advances 12500000 backward Euler
steps per case at T=1; `workers` parallelizes cases. The earlier, cheaper
run is retained under its original filename.

```{r nonzero-mean-rough-parameters}
T_final <- 1
kappa <- 0
gamma_star <- 1/3
alpha_vector <- seq(0.9,1.7,0.1)
diffusion <- 1
J_vector <- 5:9
time_step <- 8e-8
m_fixed <- 16L
reference_cutoff <- 16L
reference_J <- 18L
reference_time_step <- 5e-6
max_tail_squared_fraction <- 0.002
workers <- 9L
initial_mean <- 1
forcing_mean <- 1
graph_length <- 3
max_mean_squared_fraction <- 0.02
recompute_centered <- TRUE
centered_file <- "data_files/nonzero_mean_rough_centered_publication.rds"
output_file <- "data_files/nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat_publication.rds"

# Bundle only the visible parameters above for the shared runner.
settings <- list(study="rough_h",T_final=T_final,kappa=kappa,gamma_star=gamma_star,
    alpha=alpha_vector,diffusion=diffusion,workers=workers,J=J_vector,tau=time_step,m=m_fixed,
    cutoff=reference_cutoff,reference_J=reference_J,reference_tau=reference_time_step,
    max_tail_squared_fraction=max_tail_squared_fraction)
centered_settings <- settings
settings$initial_mean <- initial_mean
settings$forcing_mean <- forcing_mean
settings$graph_length <- graph_length
settings$max_mean_squared_fraction <- max_mean_squared_fraction
settings_table <- data.frame(parameter=names(settings),
    value=vapply(settings,function(x) paste(x,collapse=", "),character(1)))
knitr::kable(settings_table)
```

## Direct sum of the rough subspace and the constant mode

The centered solver uses the same quarter-loop interval $[0,1/2]$, zero
endpoint values, odd reflection, and period-one extension as the mean-zero
rough notebook. Four copies reconstruct the full loop; the centered
solution is zero on the stem. Its reduced mass matrix is four times the
interval mass matrix. On aligned meshes $h=2^{-J}$ the infinite forcing
has the exact FEM load $\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}j^{-1}(\phi_j,\psi_i)$; these
integrals are assembled analytically, without sampling the rough series.

A constant does not belong to that reduced space. The **total** solution
therefore lives in the direct sum of the antisymmetric subspace and the
full-graph constant space:
$$
 U_{\rm added}^k=\mathcal E U_{\rm red}^k+a_k\mathbf1,
 \qquad a_0=1,\qquad a_{k+1}=a_k+\tau,
 \qquad a_k=1+t_k.
$$
Here $\mathcal E$ is the reflection/extension operator. We evaluate this
scalar recurrence by its closed form, so no accumulated time-stepping
roundoff is introduced. BRASIL and all shifted sparse solves act only on
$U_{\rm red}^k$, with `split_mean=FALSE` there. No quarter-interval mean
is subtracted. The constant is included on **both the stem and loop**;
the total solution no longer has the centered solution's odd symmetry.

This is the paper's zero-shift mean splitting on this invariant subspace:
$\bar U^k=1+t_k$, $\bar f^k=1$, and
$F_Q^k=F^k-C\mathbf1=F_g$. Consequently the centered evolution is exactly
the saved mean-zero rough evolution. Combining it with the separate mean
is the numerical scheme itself, without another rational approximation
or a new PDE solve. The saved result records the centered result's file
hash, generation date, original source hashes, and parameters separately
from this notebook's generation date and source hashes.

## Reference solution and the measured total error

The same reference cutoff is used for the centered continuum solution:
$$
 u_K(s,t)=\sum_{j=1}^{K}\frac{1-e^{-\nu(\pi2^j)^\alpha t}}
 {j\nu(\pi2^j)^\alpha}\phi_j(s).
$$
The added reference is $u_K+1+t$. Its omitted rough tail has the same bound
$$
 B_K=\frac{T}{\nu^2\pi^{2\alpha}}
 \frac{2^{-2\alpha(K+1)}}{(K+1)^2(1-2^{-2\alpha})}.
$$
We retain the tail check against the **centered** error, so adding the
constant cannot make an inadequate rough reference appear acceptable.
Both centered and total tail fractions are reported.

The numerical reconstruction is right-constant in time: on
$(t_{k-1},t_k]$ its constant coefficient is $1+t_k$, while the reference
has $1+t$. The centered error is orthogonal to constants, including under
the consistent reference mass matrix by antisymmetry. Thus the actual
sampled error is computed exactly by
$$
 E_{\rm added}^2=E_{\rm centered}^2+
 |\Gamma|\sum_\ell w_\ell
 [\bar f(t_{k(\ell)}-t_\ell^\star)]^2,
 \qquad |\Gamma|=3,\quad\bar f=1.
$$
The weights and step indices below match `kappa0_sampled_error()`:
$w_\ell=t_\ell^\star-t_{\ell-1}^\star$ and $k(\ell)$ selects the first
solver time at or after the reference time. The factor is the full length
3, **not** the loop length 2 or quarter-loop length 1/2. For an exact time
integral and uniform steps the added squared term would be $T\tau^2$;
we instead use the study's actual sampled quadrature, preserving its norm.
The shared constant initial mean cancels from this error.

Raw errors, $J E_h$, fitted slopes, and $h^\alpha$ guides are reported as
in the mean-zero notebook. The extra temporal term can eventually cause
a floor under spatial refinement; it is retained in every total error.
`mass_by_antisymmetry=0` describes only the centered component. Total
initial/final masses and the closed-form mean recurrence are saved separately.

## Manual computation

```{r nonzero-mean-rough-recompute, eval=FALSE}
started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
if(recompute_centered) {
    for(package in c("Matrix","rSPDE","Rcpp","RcppEigen"))
        if(!requireNamespace(package,quietly=TRUE)) stop("Missing package: ",package)
    true_diff <- local({
        extracted <- tempfile("nonzero_mean_rough_",fileext=".R")
        on.exit(unlink(extracted),add=TRUE)
        knitr::purl("kappa0func.Rmd",output=extracted,quiet=TRUE,documentation=0L)
        functions <- new.env(parent=globalenv())
        sys.source(extracted,envir=functions)
        functions
    })
    centered_source <- centered_file
    centered <- true_diff$kappa0_compute_study(centered_settings,
        "nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.Rmd",centered_source)
} else {
    centered_source <- centered_file
    if(!file.exists(centered_source)) stop("Missing centered result; set recompute_centered=TRUE and run manually.")
    centered <- readRDS(centered_source)
}
scientific <- setdiff(names(centered_settings),"workers")
bad <- scientific[!vapply(scientific,function(name)
    isTRUE(all.equal(centered$parameters[[name]],centered_settings[[name]],tolerance=1e-12)),logical(1))]
if(length(bad)) stop("Centered result differs for: ",paste(bad,collapse=", "))
stopifnot(is.finite(initial_mean),is.finite(forcing_mean),graph_length==3)
# Identical time-grid and index conventions to the shared sampled solver.
N <- max(1,ceiling(T_final/time_step))
solver_times <- seq(0,T_final,length.out=N+1)
N_reference <- max(1,ceiling(T_final/reference_time_step))
reference_times <- seq(0,T_final,length.out=N_reference+1)
times <- reference_times[-1L]
targets <- findInterval(times,solver_times,left.open=TRUE)
mean_error_squared <- graph_length*sum(diff(reference_times)*
    (forcing_mean*(solver_times[targets+1L]-times))^2)
result <- centered
result$centered_provenance <- list(file=centered_source,
    md5=tools::md5sum(centered_source),generated_at=centered$generated_at,
    source_hashes=centered$source_hashes,parameters=centered$parameters,
    elapsed_seconds=centered$elapsed_seconds)
d <- result$results
d$centered_error <- d$error
d$centered_tail_squared_fraction <- d$tail_squared_fraction
stopifnot(all(d$centered_tail_squared_fraction<=max_tail_squared_fraction))
d$mean_error_squared <- mean_error_squared
d$error <- sqrt(d$centered_error^2+mean_error_squared)
d$corrected_error <- d$J*d$error
d$tail_squared_fraction <- d$cutoff_squared_bound/d$error^2
d$mean_squared_error_fraction <- mean_error_squared/d$error^2
if(any(d$mean_squared_error_fraction>max_mean_squared_fraction))
    stop("Mean error budget exceeded: reduce time_step, recompute centered PDE, and rerun.")
d$initial_mass <- graph_length*initial_mean
d$final_mass <- graph_length*(initial_mean+forcing_mean*T_final)
result$results <- d
result$rates <- do.call(rbind,lapply(alpha_vector,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]
    data.frame(alpha=a,reference=a,
        raw=unname(coef(lm(log(error)~log(axis),data=x))[2L]),
        observed=unname(coef(lm(log(corrected_error)~log(axis),data=x))[2L]))
}))
result$mean_recurrence <- list(initial=initial_mean,forcing=forcing_mean,
    graph_length=graph_length,steps=N,time_step=T_final/N,
    formula="a_k = initial_mean + forcing_mean * t_k",
    sampled_squared_error=mean_error_squared)
result$parameters <- settings
result$source_hashes <- tools::md5sum(c("kappa0func.Rmd","nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.Rmd"))
result$generated_at <- format(Sys.time(),"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z",tz="Asia/Riyadh")
result$elapsed_seconds <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]-started
result$error_definition <- "sampled full-graph continuum-reference error: centered rough error plus exact constant contribution"
dir.create(dirname(output_file),recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
saveRDS(result,output_file)
```

## Load saved results

```{r nonzero-mean-rough-load-results}
if(!file.exists(output_file)) stop("Saved result missing. Run setup, parameters, and recompute manually before knitting.")
result <- readRDS(output_file)
scientific <- setdiff(names(settings),"workers")
bad <- scientific[!vapply(scientific,function(name)
    isTRUE(all.equal(result$parameters[[name]],settings[[name]],tolerance=1e-12)),logical(1))]
if(length(bad)) stop("Saved result differs for: ",paste(bad,collapse=", "),". Recompute manually.")
cat("Added-mean result generated:",result$generated_at,
    "\nCentered full PDE run generated:",result$centered_provenance$generated_at,
    "\nCentered result:",result$centered_provenance$file,"\n")
knitr::kable(result$rates,digits=6)
cat("Sampled squared error from the mean:",result$mean_recurrence$sampled_squared_error,
    "\nLargest fraction of total squared error from the mean:",
    max(result$results$mean_squared_error_fraction),"\n")
```

## Raw and logarithmically corrected spatial convergence

```{r nonzero-mean-rough-plot-results}
d <- result$results
d$alpha_label <- factor(d$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
if (settings$study=="m") {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape=resolved))+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x="sqrt(m)",y="Isolated space-time L2 error",
            colour="alpha",shape="Resolved",title="Zero-shift rational convergence")
} else {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(axis,error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x=if(settings$study=="tau") "tau" else "h",
            y="Sampled space-time L2 error",colour="alpha",title="Zero-shift rough convergence: nonzero mean")
}
# Reference curves retain their prescribed slope and are geometrically
# anchored to the data. They are guides, not additional computed errors.
guides <- do.call(rbind,lapply(settings$alpha,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]
    power <- if(settings$study=="m") -2*pi*sqrt(a/2) else if(settings$study=="tau") 1 else 2
    xx <- if(settings$study=="m") sqrt(x$m) else log(x$axis)
    if(settings$study=="rough_h") power <- a
    x$guide <- exp(mean(log(x$error)-power*xx)+power*xx)
    x
}))
guides$alpha_label <- factor(guides$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
p <- p+ggplot2::geom_line(data=guides,ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed",alpha=0.6)+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)+ggplot2::labs(subtitle=sprintf("kappa=0; gamma*=%g",settings$gamma_star))
print(p)
figure_dir <- "data_files/nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat_publication"
dir.create(figure_dir,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"convergence.pdf"),p,width=8,height=5)
```

### Logarithmically corrected spatial errors

The raw-error plot above includes h-to-the-alpha guides for context;
the theoretical logarithmic correction is assessed in this second plot.
The corrected slopes are the `observed` column of the rate table.

```{r nonzero-mean-rough-corrected-figure}
corrected_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(axis,corrected_error,colour=alpha_label))+
    ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+
    ggplot2::labs(x="h",y="J times sampled space-time L2 error",colour="alpha")+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)
corrected_guides <- do.call(rbind,lapply(settings$alpha,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]; x$guide <- exp(mean(log(x$corrected_error)-a*log(x$axis)))*x$axis^a; x
}))
corrected_plot <- corrected_plot+ggplot2::geom_line(data=corrected_guides,
    ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed",alpha=0.6)
print(corrected_plot)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"corrected_convergence.pdf"),corrected_plot,width=8,height=5)
cat("Largest centered squared-tail fraction:",max(d$centered_tail_squared_fraction),"\n")
```

The `.rds` file contains the saved settings, errors, rates, source hashes,
package versions, and generation timestamp. Figures are redrawn from the
saved values when knitting and written to the full-run figure directory.
To change the experiment, edit its parameter chunk and run the computation
chunk manually before knitting again. Setting `NAP.true_diff.recompute`
or any previous profile option has no effect on knitting these notebooks.
Internal tests and smaller exploratory runs belong in `DOCS/NAP`, not in
these report notebooks.
